pr_title: drivers: adc: TI CC13xx/CC26xx ADC support
pr_body:
Hello, I implemented a new ADC driver for the TI CC13xx/CC26xx family.

Tested using the adc sample on my CC1352P1 LaunchXL board.
I configured the demo DTS overlay to measure the chip's VDDS voltage.

Fixes #49228

<details>
<summary>See sample logs here:</summary>

```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.1.0-3811-g3217d9737530  ***
ADC reading:
- adc@400cb008, channel 5: [03123 = 3278 mV
0:00:00.005,859] <dbg> adc_cc13xx_cc26xx: adc_cc13xx_cc26xx_channel_setup: Setup 5 acq time 9
[00:00:00.009,582] <dbg> adc_cc13xx_cc26xx: adc_cc13xx_cc26xx_isr: ISR flags 0x00000480 fifo 0x00000000
[00:00:00.009,613] <dbg> adc_cc13xx_cc26xx: adc_cc13xx_cc26xx_isr: ADC val 3123
[00:00:00.009,643] <dbg> adc_cc13xx_cc26xx: adc_cc13xx_cc26xx_isr: ISR flags 0x00000400 fifo 0x00000001
ADC reading:
- adc@400cb008, channel 5: 3124 = 3279 mV
```
</details>

Note: requires [`hal_ti` changes (PR here)](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_ti/pull/39).

Also added a separate commit updating the sample overlays + docs + yaml metadata for all supported boards.
Oh, and I updated `west.yml`'s `hal_ti` entry's commit ID, I hope this is the way to do it.
@niflostancu - can you please rebase? Should be good to go in
Thanks. I will update my PR tomorrow ;)
Done: rebased, applied all of @anangl's suggestions, re-tested on my launchxls, nothing broken ;)
@niflostancu - CI is getting `#error unsupported board` - is something else missing in CMake or possibly in the HAL?

Well, it seems that the tests in `adc_api` have hardcoded `if defined(CONFIG_BOARD_*)` conditions for all supported boards :D 
Added CC1352R* branch in there (new commit), tests should pass now ;)

> Well, it seems that the tests in `adc_api` have hardcoded `if defined(CONFIG_BOARD_*)` conditions for all supported boards :D Added CC1352R* branch in there (new commit), tests should pass now ;)

Almost - I would suggest running tests with `twister` before pushing
```
twister -b -p cc1352r1_launchxl -p cc1352r_sensortag -p cc26x2r1_launchxl -p cc3220sf_launchxl -p cc3235sf_launchxl -T tests/drivers/adc
```

Yep, I've just discovered `--device-testing` and I've been trying to pass the ADC tests on my CC1352* LaunchXL (instead of the sample, which worked).

I get this:
```
Running TESTSUITE adc_basic
===================================================================
START - test_adc_asynchronous_call
Samples read: 0x0c35 0xffff8000
Assertion failed at WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/tests/drivers/adc/adc_api/src/test_adc.c:467: check_samples: (INVALID_ADC_VALUE equal to sample_value)
[1] should be filled
FAIL - test_adc_asynchronous_call in 0.020 seconds
```

It seems it's only sampling the first time, it probably gets interrupted, I need to further investigate the driver for why this happens.

Unfortunately, I'll have to postpone this until next week since I'll be going AFK for several days.

Good luck - looking forward to seeing this land.

All right, it's fixed:

```
DEBUG   - DEVICE: ------ TESTSUITE SUMMARY START ------
DEBUG   - DEVICE:
DEBUG   - DEVICE: SUITE PASS - 100.00% [adc_basic]: pass = 5, fail = 0, skip = 1, total = 6 duration = 0.550 seconds
DEBUG   - DEVICE: - PASS - [adc_basic.test_adc_asynchronous_call] duration = 0.008 seconds
DEBUG   - DEVICE: - PASS - [adc_basic.test_adc_invalid_request] duration = 0.017 seconds
DEBUG   - DEVICE: - PASS - [adc_basic.test_adc_repeated_samplings] duration = 0.104 seconds
DEBUG   - DEVICE: - PASS - [adc_basic.test_adc_sample_one_channel] duration = 0.009 seconds
DEBUG   - DEVICE: - SKIP - [adc_basic.test_adc_sample_two_channels] duration = 0.001 seconds
DEBUG   - DEVICE: - PASS - [adc_basic.test_adc_sample_with_interval] duration = 0.411 seconds
DEBUG   - DEVICE:
DEBUG   - DEVICE: ------ TESTSUITE SUMMARY END ------
...
INFO    - 1/1 cc1352r1_launchxl         tests/drivers/adc/adc_api/drivers.adc              PASSED (device 6.100s)
```

The bug was stupid: the sampling buffer was double incremented, once by `adc_context_update_buffer_pointer` and, wrongly, by `adc_cc13xx_cc26xx_isr`:
```c
*data->buffer++ = adc_value;
```

I removed the latter's incrementation op.
I probably saw this in HAL TI's official ADC driver and thought it belonged there :(

issue_context.title: ti: cc13xx_cc26xx: ADC support
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, TI CC13xx/CC26xx lacks ADC drivers.

I am currently working on a new ADC driver for this family, PR incoming ;)

Thanks.

review_comments: Since you are using `(adc_cc13xx_sample_times[i].time_us > sample_time_us)` in the loop below, this should be 171 (and similarly for the next 6 entries). But it actually seems that using `>=` in the condition and floor rounding of the values would be clearer.
